sections.transcript: On the agenda for yesterday's City Council meeting was yet another discussion of the public transit dilemma. Over the past 15 years, this city has experienced a significant growth in population, a trend expected to continue well into the future. As a result of this growth, the public transit system, designed with a much smaller population in mind, has been operating beyond its capacity. As an example, Thomas Findley commutes from Glenfield to downtown on a daily basis. While a year ago, it took him 35 minutes to arrive at work by bus, the time frame today is more in the realm of one hour and 35 minutes. For Findley, this is unacceptable. He contends that the delays stem from an increase in public transit users without a corresponding increase in the number of buses. The result? Buses are often full to capacity and riders must wait long periods before one with space will stop for more passengers. As a solution, Findley has suggested doubling the number of buses in operation. However, transit planner Rita Cummings argues that this would only be a temporary fix. she insists that increasing the number of buses would lead to significantly more traffic, something which, in the long run, could cause both greater delays as well as an increase in air pollution. Instead, comings has proposed the construction of a subway system. Since subways run underground, a large number of commuters can be moved without a corresponding increase in traffic. Consequently, comings Things feels that for growing cities, a subway system is almost always the most efficient and environmentally sound choice. She noted that subways in Toronto and Montreal have successfully fulfilled their roles for decades, each now carrying more than a million passengers every day. In contrast, while City Councilor Scott Dresden agrees a subway is a nice idea, he questions whether the need truly justifies the expense. According to Dresden, the cost of developing a subway system could easily run into the billions. Although the city's population is growing, it is unlikely to ever reach the numbers to warrant such an expense. As an alternative, Dresden has suggested the purchase of modern, efficiently designed buses which have the capacity to carry double the number of passengers. This option, Dresden asserts, would lead to neither an increase in traffic nor a breaking of the bank. In the days to come, Council will need to find a solution, be it subway, bigger buses, or maintaining the status quo, its election year, so it's anyone's guess what Council will do to curry favor.

paragraphs: Dear Mr. Casio,

I am writing in response to the letter I received this morning. First of all, I would like to tell you that I've enjoyed living in Minto Heights this past year and would like to stay another year. However, your letter says the new rent will be $1,500 a month. This is a big increase from the $1,100 I have been paying. Could we come to an agreement that both of us can accept?

My online research tells me that the rent increase is legal, but the price is unusual. A similar apartment (two bedrooms, 1,300 square feet, 5 years old, one underground parking spot) typically rents for $1,000 per month. This is less than what I'm paying now. In fact, most similar apartments include air conditioning, but mine doesn't.

I read in the newspaper that 4.1% of city apartments are empty this year and 4.4% will be vacant next year. This isn't surprising, as there are currently 200 new condominium buildings under construction in the city. Good tenants are valuable and hard to find. That's why I think you should charge the same rent next year. If you raise the rent, you might find someone willing to pay $400 more. However, it is equally possible that you will have an empty apartment earning zero income.

I feel that I am the type of tenant you would like to keep. I have always paid my rent on time. I haven't damaged the apartment. I don't smoke or play loud music, and I follow the "no pets" rule. I have always shovelled the snow off my balcony, as required in the lease. In addition, I have shovelled the front walkway, even though I'm not required to. This has helped to keep your other tenants safe.

If you agree to renew my lease at the current monthly rate, I will pay the first 3 months' rent in cash right away and the remainder in postdated cheques. Could you kindly let me know before May 1st if this is acceptable?
Sincerely,
Deborah Perrault

paragraphs: A. 2015 was a big year for all of Canada. Toronto hosted both the Pan American and the Parapan American Games. The Games are one of the largest multi-sport events in the world, along with the Olympic Summer Games and the Asian Games. The Pan American Games (also known as the Pan Am Games) offer opportunities for thousands of top-notch athletes from North, Central, and South America and the Caribbean to compete in a variety of summer sports. The Parapan American Games welcome athletes with physical disabilities. The Games offer great pageantry, excitement, and sportsmanship to sports fans and residents alike.

B. The Pan Am Games started in 1951 in Buenos Aires, Argentina. The first Parapan Am Games were held in Mexico City in 1999. The Games have grown in size with each passing year: participation has increased from 2,500 athletes representing 14 nations at the first competition to over 6,000 contenders from 41 countries at the last games. Both the Pan Am and Parapan Am Games take place every four years, in the year before the Summer Olympics and Paralympic Games. Thirty-six sports (eight more than the official Olympic sports) are now featured at the Games. Pan Am sports not found at the Olympics include bowling, karate, baseball, and squash.

C. The celebration of the Pan American Games features such rituals and emblems as its own flag, torch, and anthem, in addition to opening and closing ceremonies. Each event also has a mascotan animal or human figure representing the cultural heritage of the host country. This helps to create a distinct identity and promote the Games. The official mascot of the Toronto Games was Pachi the Porcupine, an animal native to Canada. His depiction was created by a group of eighth grade students from Markham, Ontario. Four friends put their heads together, spent two months perfecting their porcupine, and won the highly competitive Mascot Creation Challenge.

D. The 2015 Games were not the first for Canada; Winnipeg, Manitoba, has welcomed renowned athletes from the Americas twice in the past. The most recent Pan Am and Parapan Am Games brought in over 10,000 athletes, coaches, and delegates, along with as many as 250,000 visitors who came to cheer them on. This major international event created immense opportunities for all Canadians, helping to showcase Toronto and Ontario to an international audience, as well as attracting tourists, developing jobs, and encouraging new business investment. Beyond 2015, the Games will provide housing, transportation, educational, and recreational legacies for decades to come.
E. Not given in any of the above paragraphs.

paragraphs: A Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) is a constructive means for an employer to provide an underperforming employee with the opportunity to regain good standing in the company. A PIP outlines measurable criteria for improved performance and sets deadlines for meeting said criteria. It also presents actions the employer will take to support the employee in reaching the PIP targets.

Nonetheless, not everyone views PIPs as well-intentioned. According to David Brown, HR manager at a leading recruiting agency, "PIPs might as well be called 'first step toward firing plans.' Employers use PIPs as a tool to initiate an employee's dismissal. In effect, companies shield themselves from liability by creating a paper trail of evidence that can be used against an employee in the case of termination. If you have been given a PIP, the company has made up its mind. It's time to polish your resumé and start job hunting."

Jane Doris, a seasoned corporate manager, disagrees, emphasizing that PIPs clearly demonstrate a company's commitment to an employee. "If your management has grounds for terminating your contract, they usually simply carry out that decision. If instead they invest their time in a PIP, they likely want to give you a chance." In some cases, the problem is caused by the individual's lack of training or by a lack of transparency regarding the employer's expectations. Doris goes on to say that this is where the solution lies. "By simply clarifying performance requirements, employees on PIPs are given time to prove themselves."

Those who are determined to succeed after a PIP may want to heed the advice of Demi Vazquez, CEO of KC Hiring Solutions: "At the outset, you should make sure your PIP goals are transparent and free of any ambiguity. Then, ask about resources like coaching or literature that could help you achieve your PIP goals. You might also consider asking your overachieving colleagues about their secrets for acing their daily responsibilities. Finally, track your progress daily and share it with your manager in regularly scheduled meetings."

paragraphs: Unlike David Brown, I firmly believe that employees should look at PIPs as a {{6}}. Having been on the receiving end, however, I have to side with Brown. As Brown suggests, after receiving a PIP, I was {{9}}. This ended up being the best thing for my career. So here's my advice: if you're ever given a PIP, forget about Vazquez's {{10}} Your dream job could be just around the corner! Jesse Donovan

tasks.title: Writing an Email
scenario: You are a college student. Your school is offering $2,000 to one student: this money will be used to pay college fees. The school is inviting all students to explain why they should get this award.
tasks.instruction: Write an email of about 150-200 words to the college. Your email must include the following points:
bullets: a description of what you are studying at college
why you are interested in your studies
a statement of how well you are doing at college

tasks.title: Responding to Survey Questions
scenario: Your college is surveying your opinion about evening class schedules. Currently, evening classes are offered once per week, 3 hours each class. The college is considering changing the schedule to two evenings per week, 1.5 hours each class. The college has asked you to complete an opinion survey.
tasks.instruction: Choose the option that you prefer. Why do you prefer your choice? Explain the reasons for your choice. Write about 150-200 words.
options: Option A: I want to keep my current schedule of 3-hour classes, once per week.
Option B: I want to change my schedule to 1.5-hour classes, twice per week.

tasks.title: Practice Task
prompt: Talk about one of your best friends.

tasks.title: Giving Advice
prompt: Your friend has to work with a classmate on a school project. The classmate doesn't do any work, so your friend does everything. Your friend feels upset and angry. Advise your friend about what he should do to solve this problem.

tasks.title: Talking about a Personal Experience
prompt: Talk about a time you participated in a program. Maybe you can talk about a time you participated in a language program, an art workshop, or a summer camp. What was the program, what did you do, and why did you want to participate?

tasks.title: Describing a Scene
prompt: Describe some things that are happening in the picture below as well as you can. The person with whom you are speaking cannot see the picture.

tasks.title: Making Predictions
prompt: In this picture, what do you think will most likely happen next?

tasks.title: Comparing and Persuading
selectPrompt: You and your friend Daniel are looking for a place to sit down and enjoy a drink. You found two suitable options. Using the pictures and information below, choose the option that you prefer. In the next section, you will need to persuade Daniel that your choice is the better choice.
If you do not choose an option, the computer will choose one for you. You do not need to speak for this part.
prompt: Daniel is suggesting a nearby lemonade stand. Persuade him that the location you chose is more suitable by comparing the two.

tasks.title: Dealing with a Difficult Situation
prompt: You have recently started a new job. An employee at your new workplace is retiring and a colleague, Ming, has asked everyone to chip in $30 for a retirement gift. However, you do not know the person who is retiring and your spouse believes that you should not spend this much money on a gift for a stranger.
choices: Talk to Ming. Explain why you should not have to chip in any money for a retirement gift.
Talk to your spouse. Explain why you should chip in the money for a retirement gift.

tasks.title: Expressing Opinions
prompt: Answer the following question and give reasons for your answer. Question: Do you think high school graduates should work for a while before going to university? Explain your reasons.

tasks.title: Describing an Unusual Situation
prompt: You are at a festival downtown, and you see an interesting parade. Your friend Gloria likes parades. Call Gloria, describe in detail what the parade looks like, and ask her if she would like to come and see it.
